reasons: Fixed IDs make all schedules look identical.

terms.meaning: a way of sending a file inside a web request
a starting number that makes random results repeatable
a measure of how many tasks have very little slack

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the router, ID type, upload and file tools, request checking and the database session.
sections.why: Likely reason: the endpoints below need these tools.
sections.watch_out: The upload tool needs a separate add-on library, and without it the file endpoint may fail at startup.

sections.name: IngestScheduleResponse
sections.title: Import reply shape
sections.what: Describes the import reply: schedule ID, number of activities and baseline duration in days.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms what was imported.
sections.watch_out: The ID returned is fixed, so it cannot be used to find the real import.

sections.name: CPMResponse
sections.title: Critical path reply shape
sections.what: Describes the critical path reply: duration, critical and near-critical task counts, and fragility.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets the summary numbers a caller receives.
sections.watch_out: Fragility is a plain decimal here, while the database describes it as a percentage, so units may disagree.

sections.name: MonteCarloRequest
sections.title: Risk run request shape
sections.what: Describes a risk run request: schedule ID, trial count defaulting to 10000, and seed defaulting to 42.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets a default run size and repeatable randomness.
sections.watch_out: The fixed default seed makes repeat runs identical, which helps testing but can hide variation.

sections.name: MonteCarloResponse
sections.title: Risk percentile reply shape
sections.what: Describes the risk reply with 50, 80 and 90 percent finish durations in days.
sections.why: Likely reason: the standard confidence levels used in schedule reviews.
sections.watch_out: The reply gives durations, while the database stores finish dates, so the two must be converted.

sections.name: RCPSPResponse
sections.title: Alternative plans reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply as a list of alternative plan entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: a flexible list while the plan fields are still being settled.
sections.watch_out: Entries are untyped, so each field must be checked by the caller.

sections.name: ingest_schedule
sections.title: Schedule import endpoint
sections.what: Accepts an uploaded schedule file and a project ID, and returns a fixed schedule ID, 150 activities and a 365 day baseline without reading the file.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until file parsing is written.
sections.watch_out: The uploaded file is ignored, so a bad file also appears to succeed.

sections.name: run_cpm
sections.title: Critical path endpoint
sections.what: Returns fixed critical path results: 365 days, 45 critical tasks, 12 near-critical tasks and a fragility of 0.38.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until the critical path calculation exists.
sections.watch_out: The schedule ID is not used, so any ID, even a wrong one, gets the same results.

sections.name: run_monte_carlo
sections.title: Risk simulation endpoint
sections.what: Returns fixed 50, 80 and 90 percent durations of 365, 395 and 420 days, ignoring the trial count and seed.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until the simulation exists.
sections.watch_out: The trial count and seed have no effect, so a larger run appears to give better results when nothing changed.

sections.name: run_rcpsp
sections.title: Alternative plans endpoint
sections.what: Returns two fixed alternative plans with duration changes and indirect cost savings, not generated from the schedule.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until the scheduling optimizer exists. The docstring describes the intended method.
sections.watch_out: The savings are fixed figures, so presenting them as results would mislead.

summary: Exposes endpoints to import a schedule file and to run critical path, risk simulation and resource-constrained scheduling, all returning fixed example numbers.
purpose: A planned API for schedule analysis of solar construction projects.
why: Likely reason: the routes are set up first for front end work. The placeholder comments say so.
how: 1) The import endpoint accepts an uploaded file and returns a fixed schedule ID and counts. 2) The critical path, risk simulation and scenario endpoints each return fixed results without reading the schedule.
inputs: An uploaded schedule file for import. A schedule or project ID, and for risk runs a trial count and seed.
outputs: Fixed counts, durations, percentiles and scenarios.
risks: Every result looks real but is constant. The uploaded file is not read. The schedule ID is fixed, so every import looks the same.
debug: If numbers never change, these are placeholders. If upload fails, check that the multipart upload library is installed.
